note:
Header banner for /pages/shipping-returns. Like /pages/contact, the hero has NO IMAGE AT ALL today — verified on the live theme 2026-08-30: templates/page.shipping-returns.json section `hero` (image-with-text-overlay) carries no `image` and no `mobile_image`, so it paints flat #1A1A1A at overlay_opacity 100 with centred white type over 'Shipping & Returns' and the free-shipping subline.

Malcolm's brief, 2026-08-30: 'a close up of a woman receiving a white box package from a delivery man. You only see the back of the postman's head.'

THE WHITE BOX IS THE RISK IN THIS WAVE, and it is the reason the negatives are longer here than on the contact banner. A plain white carton is exactly the surface every engine wants to fill: a shipping label, a barcode, a courier logo, an address block, fragile arrows. FLUX.2 in particular prints characters and digits unasked — it put graduation numbers on lab glassware on all three waves of 2026-08-25 despite being told not to, and it is the only engine that does. So the box is described positively as UNPRINTED in every slot, negated by every name a printed element goes by, and every candidate must be checked at full size before it can be chosen. A garbled courier logo on a shipping page is an invented brand, not a cosmetic defect.

SAME TRAP ON THE UNIFORM. A courier uniform invites a DHL/UPS/PostNL-alike mark. Every slot puts the delivery driver in plain unbranded workwear and negates the chest and cap.

HANDS ARE THE SECOND RISK. Two people and a box handed between them is the classic malformed-hand shot. Every slot states five fingers explicitly and keeps the grip simple — flat palms under the box, not fingers wrapped over an edge.

GEOMETRY. Generated at 3072x1280 (2.4:1), the page-break band spec, then extended with scripts/extend-banner-canvas.py to ~4.42:1 so full height survives a 1920 viewport. The box is a fixed PIXEL height (375/400/440px full-bleed), not an aspect ratio.

TYPE ZONE IS THE LEFT 45 PERCENT, measured as a fraction of frame width, matching /pages/the-science and the collection banners. So the exchange sits RIGHT and the postman enters from the RIGHT edge — the back of his head is the nearest thing to camera, which is what Malcolm asked for, and it keeps the busiest part of the picture away from the headline.

⚠️ The left 45 percent is specified as CONTINUOUS SPACE — a softly out-of-focus hallway or doorway interior, evenly lit — deliberately NOT as 'quiet and almost empty'. That exact phrasing produced a hard black bar across a model's forehead on all five engines on the FAQ macro. Say what reaches the edges.

NO REFERENCE IMAGE IS SENT (class B). Nothing branded is in frame; the box is deliberately anonymous. Class B may route to FLUX.2, but see the box warning above — check it at full size, not on the contact sheet.

defaults.negative_global: text, lettering, printed characters, numbers, digits, barcode, QR code, shipping label, address label, postage stamp, franking mark, courier logo, brand mark, company name, chest logo, cap badge, fragile symbol, arrow symbol, this-way-up marking, watermark, signature, border, collage, multi-panel, cartoon, illustration, 3d render, plastic waxy airbrushed skin, extra fingers, malformed hands, six fingers

slots.title: At her door, taking the box, postman's head-back at the right edge
slots.prompt:
A photorealistic wide editorial photograph, 2.4:1 letterbox format, of a woman taking delivery of a parcel at the open door of her home.

The woman is in her late thirties with fair skin and dark shoulder-length hair, wearing a plain oatmeal knit jumper with no pattern and no visible fastening. She stands on the right of the frame, her head and shoulders from about 0.58 to 0.80 of the frame width and from about 0.14 to 0.76 of the frame height, looking down at the parcel she is receiving with a warm, pleased, natural smile. Her face is in sharp focus and she shows real, unretouched skin — visible pores, fine lines at the outer eye, faint natural colour variation — lit so texture is present without being emphasised.

She is taking a small square carton with both hands, flat palms supporting it from beneath, her fingers relaxed and not wrapped over the top edge. Each hand has exactly five fingers, correctly proportioned. The carton sits low in the frame, from about 0.60 to 0.80 of the frame width and from about 0.62 to 0.90 of the frame height. It is a plain matte white cardboard box, completely blank and unprinted on every visible face — no label, no writing, no symbol, no barcode, no tape print, no mark of any kind. Its surfaces are smooth white card with soft natural shading that shows the edges of the box.

At the right edge of the frame, nearest the camera, the delivery driver is seen only from behind: the back of his head and one shoulder, cropped by the right edge, entering from the bottom edge and reaching up to about 0.66 of the frame height and inward to about 0.95 of the frame width. He has short dark hair and wears a plain slate-grey polo shirt that is completely unbranded — no logo, no printing, no badge, no name. He is rendered soft and out of focus. No part of his face is visible at any point.

Lighting is bright, soft, natural daylight from the open doorway on the right, giving gentle directional modelling on the woman's face and no hard shadow edges.

The left 45 percent of the frame, measured from 0 to 0.45 of frame width, is the interior of her hallway behind her, thrown well out of focus: a clean pale space in warm off-white and soft grey, evenly lit at a mid tone, holding gentle continuous gradation with no dark band, no vignette and no abrupt change of tone anywhere. It is soft and simple enough for a headline to sit on it unaided, but it is a real hallway and not an empty void. Nothing in it reads as a recognisable object, and there is no signage, artwork, character or symbol anywhere in the picture. The hallway fills the frame all the way to the top edge, the bottom edge and the left edge.

Colour is calm and warm-neutral: white, warm off-white, soft grey, oatmeal, and natural skin tones only. Shot on a full-frame camera with an 85mm lens at f/2.2, natural colour, no filter, magazine-quality editorial photography.
slots.negative_extra: no clipboard, no handheld scanner, no phone, no delivery van, no letterbox, no house number, no doormat lettering
